title: cloud/factory vitest emits a wall of workerd hung-context exceptions
description:
Surfaced by xrz. cloud/factory pnpm exec vitest run reports 13/13 files and 252/252 green while emitting a wall of uncaught workerd exceptions (io-context.c++:1593 ... code had hung). Pre-existing — the tick author reports their own new file produces none.

Why it is worth a tick rather than tolerating: the noise is more than enough to hide a real failure in a CI log, and this suite is the factorys only automated guard. A green run nobody reads carefully is a guard in name only.

Find which suite leaves a request unresolved. 79x already recorded the likely shape: a test that ignites a run and never ends it keeps the Workflow supervising, and the next test file in the shared workerd runtime inherits the mess — that report recommends ending every run a test starts (process.exit(0); await settled(runID)).
notes:
2026-08-25 14:19 - PRIORITISED TO LEAD THE EPIC (2026-08-25). This is no longer cosmetic noise — the flake now makes the gate untrustworthy in BOTH directions and it cost a wrong conclusion today.

Evidence: the same file (cloud/factory/test/run-workflow.test.ts) failed 4, then 5, then 9, then 6 tests across four consecutive full-suite runs on one machine, always as 5s TIMEOUTS, while passing 83/83 in isolation. In CI the signal inverted — pre-merge main FAILED the factory job while the post-merge commit SUCCEEDED, and a plain rerun of an identical commit turned fail into pass. The logs are full of 'the Workers runtime canceled this request because it detected that your Worker's code had hung'.

I read that coin flip as causation twice in one session: first calling PR #62's CI failure 'staleness', then calling #62 'the culprit'. Both wrong. A gate that answers differently on identical code does not just add noise, it manufactures false findings — and every other tick in this epic is verified by that gate.

So this runs FIRST, and the other implementation ticks are blocked behind it.
2026-09-02 13:34 - Closed 2026-09-02 as legacy (Peter: no cycles on the old world). Superseded by project hzm (ticfac). See the note on 4ik for where the new implementation solves this by design.
acceptance_criteria: cloud/factory vitest runs clean with no uncaught workerd exceptions; the suite that left a request unresolved is named and fixed; the tests still pass.
